label: GitHub Code 2025 — Python
description: Real-world GitHub Python source files (the "content" field), streamed and sampled to 5,000 documents from a 55-language, 143M-row code corpus.
highlight: Surfaced a real bug, not just a data quirk: a Python file embedding real HTML (a Qt "About" dialog's setHtml(...) call) fooled the HTML-document detector into running trafilatura on the whole file, which confidently extracted an unrelated fragment and silently discarded most of the actual code. Fixed with a new --content-hint not-html flag that bypasses ALL tag-stripping for known-code sources — even the "lightweight" tier was unsafe, since <...> in code is often a Flask route param, a chained comparison, or a generic, not markup. Separately, ~99.5% of documents are correctly classified as "code" by the content-type heuristic (compare to ~90% on the math dataset), and its ghost-token hits are almost all code that legitimately manipulates tokenizer special tokens (checking for <|endoftext|>, mocking a tokenizer's <bos>/<eos>) rather than contamination — except [prompt] and [cls], which are false positives from Python identifiers that happen to collide with the ghost-token vocabulary (a list literal and a class-method parameter, not special tokens).
facts: 28.9M rows (Python config); 143.7M rows across all 55 languages
